content.comment_body: Hello everyone, Has anyone implemented ModBus TCP protocol between a [product_name] [version_no] as server and a client (a PC running ModBus Doctor)? It seems fairly simple, but after repeated tests, I keep encountering a "Time Out" issue and can’t establish communication. Does anyone have the ModBus mapping for the [product_name] [version_no]? Are there any [document]s or tutorials available that explain the configuration? I would appreciate any guidance. [user_name]

Are you familiar with the manual for the newer [product_name] [version_no]? There is an online help resource from [product_name] Soft Comfort dated 07/2016, and a [product_name] manual from the same edition.

Thanks for the pointers, but unfortunately there’s not much information regarding ModBus TCP. I can now read Digital Inputs, but I'm unable to read or write Digital Outputs. A mapping table that lists the address of each variable would be very helpful. Wishing you a pleasant evening. [user_name]
Did you really search all resources so quickly and still couldn't find the information in the online help?
Apologies, you’re right. I just checked page 59 and found the table I needed. Everything is working now. Thank you very much! [user_name]

Please note: When migrating a network project to a [version_no] device or creating a new network project for it, you are required to save with the .mnp extension due to the ModBus connection. For diagram mode, .lsc files can be used for older and current devices. Additionally, if you use online features with [version_no], it often helps to run a “determine [product_name]” function first, otherwise some online functions may fail to display results or might cause software errors.

analysis.insight_summary: Users initially encountered difficulties setting up ModBus TCP communication between a [product_name] [version_no] and a PC client, largely due to unclear or incomplete documentation, especially about variable mapping and address tables. Referring to the manual helped resolve the communication issue for one user, but the discussion highlighted further technical challenges like project migration, compatibility with certain file formats, and discrepancies in register mappings when integrating with specific SCADA software. Clear instructions and reliable documentation are crucial for successful implementation.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect a straightforward, well-documented process for configuring ModBus TCP on [product_name] [version_no], including accessible mapping tables for I/O variables and consistent data handling. They also desire current resources or tutorials to simplify setup and troubleshooting.
